AMD.short: On November 18, 2026, AMD's board amended the company's bylaws, effective immediately. The changes add stricter procedures and disclosure rules for stockholder director nominations and proposals, let the company disregard noncompliant nominee votes, require non-white proxy cards, and update the legal forum rules.

short.AMD: These are all opinion pieces from one outlet, and the only concrete events are a short-seller report and a large fund's exit. Hunterbrook alleged heavy China exposure, which AMD denied, and Coatue sold its entire stake. The pieces disagree: some call the roughly 30% to 35% drop a buying chance, while others stress valuation and China risk.
short.NVDA: Nvidia's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang less than two weeks after his resignation, and the stock jumped about 31% on Nov. 23 before giving back some of it the next day. Probes into its accounting and China dealings continue, with Huang due to meet Congress Dec. 1. Nearly all coverage is opinion, and writers disagree on whether the sell-off is a bargain or a warning.
short.META: All four articles are opinion pieces, so no new company event is reported. They mostly point back to Meta's Q3 2026 results, with ad revenue up 26% year over year. One piece stresses heavy AI spending of $135-145 billion projected for 2026, negative free cash flow in Q3 and big legal charges, while others stay upbeat, so the views differ.
